own_solution.law: For Helmholtz resonance, f = c/(2π) sqrt(A/(V Leff)), with A = πa² and Leff = l + 2βa. Here A = 4.52389×10^-4 m², V = 0.0015 m³ and Leff = 0.0604 m. The neck-plug mass is ρA Leff and the acoustic stiffness is ρc²A²/V, so density cancels.
assumptions: Small-amplitude acoustic oscillations under the stated rigid-plug and adiabatic-cavity model.
The neck and cavity contain the same equilibrium air.
The stated flask volume is the cavity volume.
A current extension increases the neck length while preserving its bore and the specified end-correction rule.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: TF775 and T8378 omit the extension number and unit retained in the other extension variants, contrary to the review requirement that variants concerning the same quantity preserve both.

counterexamples: TF775 specifies only a short extension, while its numbered twin TF909 specifies 3.2 cm.
T8378 specifies only a short extension, while its numbered twin T19EB specifies 3.2 cm.
notes: All physical classifications, dependency relations and certified numerical answers are correct. Current extensions of 1.7, 3.2 and 6.3 cm give approximately 107.759, 98.6254 and 85.3429 Hz, respectively. Earlier-run extensions and extensions of the separate funnel do not affect the present resonance. Density cancels at every listed positive value because sound speed is supplied. Both explicitly named minimal pairs preserve 3.2 cm and change the intended attachment or measurement context. Pass 2 explains that TF775 and T8378 deliberately omit numerals; this makes their metadata accurate but does not satisfy the frozen review instruction requiring the same number and unit across variants of the same quantity. I therefore retain the pass-1 structural defect; there is no physics or numerical defect.
